abstract: Manages autonomous camp electrical microgrids, field shelters, and equipment staging mass
system_message:
You are Expedition infrastructure manager (CAMP). The expedition infrastructure manager (CAMP) oversees autonomous camp electrical microgrids, field shelter setups, and heavy equipment staging mass.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Potable water production（WATER）
information_points.content:
CAMP-WATER-KPK：For the Mackenzie Valley Paleosol Corridor, hydration plant testing indicates a daily snowmelt meltwater yield of 900 L of potable water.
CAMP-WATER-W2E：For the Peel Plateau Thermokarst Route, the daily snowmelt meltwater yield from the base camp snowmelt melter skid is 400 L per twenty-four-hour period.
CAMP-WATER-9U3：For the Lac de Gras Kimberlite Transect, base camp snowmelt melter testing logs record a daily snowmelt meltwater yield of 650 L of nominal potable water production.

information_points.title: Manages autonomous camp electrical microgrids, field shelters, and equipment staging mass（BASE）
information_points.content:
CAMP-BASE-F76：For the Peel Plateau Thermokarst Route, the autonomous camp power autonomy is rated at 21 d of continuous operation without external fuel resupply, and the auxiliary shelter module mass comes to 1050 kg across the insulated four-season sleeping and laboratory tents.
CAMP-BASE-QYM：For the Lac de Gras Kimberlite Transect, the field camp generator and battery bank system provides an autonomous camp power autonomy of 18 d without external fuel resupply, and cargo weighing certificates confirm an auxiliary shelter module mass of 1050 kg for the bundled frame, insulation liners, and floor modules.
CAMP-BASE-OH3：For the Mackenzie Valley Paleosol Corridor, camp microgrid engineering assessments establish an autonomous camp power autonomy of 10 d supported without external fuel resupply, while the auxiliary shelter module mass totals 800 kg for the bundled tent kit.
